scope: Prompt adaptation for image models other than Gemini. Gemini/Nano Banana stays in gemini-image-models.json, Template N and the Studio. This file records what each vendor's official pages say about prompting, negative prompts, native parameters and editing. It records no paid calls.

status_meaning.VERIFIED: Read in a primary vendor page on the date shown; the sentence or field is quoted or paraphrased from that page.
status_meaning.PARTIAL: Read only in a secondary summary, in a page that did not render, or in an older version of the page. Use with care and check before relying on it.
status_meaning.UNKNOWN: Not found in any page read. Nothing is assumed.

mechanism_meaning.flag: Negative content is given as a parameter inside the prompt text.
mechanism_meaning.field: Negative content is a separate API or UI field.
mechanism_meaning.none: No negative field is documented in the pages read. Exclusions must be written as text in the prompt, or as positive descriptions.
mechanism_meaning.ui-only: A negative field exists in the product interface, but the API field is not available for the model named.
mechanism_meaning.unknown: Not documented in the pages read.

targets.name: Midjourney

access.api: not covered: no API page read
access.ui: Midjourney web and Discord; parameters are typed in the prompt bar

prompt_style.text: Short and simple prompts typically generate the best images. Use phrases that clearly describe what you want to see; avoid long lists or detailed instructions, which can confuse the process (Prompt Basics). The page does not say whether descriptors are comma-separated: the renderer uses commas as its own convention.

negative_prompt.text: --no lists what to leave out. Each word after --no is read separately by the moderation system, so '--no modern clothing' is read as 'no modern' and 'no clothing'. Name the clothing you want instead. Same effect as weighting part of a multi-prompt at -0.5.

text_in_image.text: No text-rendering guidance was found in the pages read. Put the wording in quotes, and check the output.

references.text: An image can go into the prompt with text or on its own: one image with text, or several images without text (Image Prompts). In Discord the image URL goes at the beginning of the text prompt. Style references and Moodboards are separate features.

edit.text: The Edit model (--edit with image URLs, up to four) changes an image from written instructions, combines up to four images, or edits regions in the Editor. Compatible with V8.1 and V8.2. Not compatible with --tile. The output matches the first image's aspect ratio unless --ar is set.

native_settings.name: --ar
native_settings.values: W:H, whole numbers only (1.39:1 is written 139:100)

native_settings.name: --no
native_settings.values: comma-separated list

native_settings.name: --raw
native_settings.values: flag: 'Gain more control over your images with Raw Mode' (Parameter List)

native_settings.name: --sref
native_settings.values: image URL or style code; 'random' creates a code

native_settings.name: --sw
native_settings.values: 0 to 1000, default 100; not with Moodboards

native_settings.name: --edit
native_settings.values: image URLs, up to four

native_settings.name: --v
native_settings.values: current default V8.2 (since 2026-07-24)

native_settings.name: --hd / --sd
native_settings.values: HD gives 2K images on V8.1; costs 1.3 GPU minutes against 0.8 for SD

limitations: The product is Discord and the web app. No API page was read, so no API fields are listed.
--style raw (an older form in earlier notes) is not in the current parameter list; the flag is --raw.
--oref is replaced by the Edit model in V8.X.
The Editor on the web uses the Edit Model for inpainting and outpainting in V8.X (Editor page, read 2026-10-14).
Image Prompts in Discord take the URL at the start of the text prompt; the API is not covered by the pages read.

targets.name: GPT Image 2.5 (OpenAI API)

access.api: Image API (images.generate, images.edit) and Responses API image_generation tool
access.ui: ChatGPT Images is a product and was not read; its behaviour is not covered here

prompt_style.text: For complex requests, organise the prompt as scene, subject, details and constraints, using labelled sections. Describe visible details: materials, lighting, colours, medium. Specify framing, viewpoint and placement. Treat camera terms as cues for appearance.

negative_prompt.text: No negative field is documented. The guide says to state exclusions in the prompt, for example 'no extra text, no watermarks, no unrelated logos'.

text_in_image.text: Put required wording in quotes and describe its position and typography. Spell unusual words letter by letter when needed. Ask for no extra text, then check spelling. Use quality medium or high for small or dense text.

references.text: Identify each input by number and purpose (subject, style, clothing, background), and say how the inputs combine. The Image API takes input images for edits; the Responses API keeps conversation context for iteration.

edit.text: Say 'change only X' and list what to preserve (identity, geometry, layout, lighting, labels). Repeated edits can drift: restate the constraints each time. For pixel-identical regions, composite the approved edit into the original, because prompting alone does not guarantee it.

native_settings.name: model
native_settings.values: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst (precise editing), gpt-image-2.5-flare (fast) in the generation guide; gpt-image-2 appears in the prompting guide table and gpt-image-1.5 in the edit reference examples

native_settings.name: size
native_settings.values: 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536 recommended; custom WIDTHxHEIGHT: multiples of 16, aspect between 1:3 and 3:1, edges up to 3840, total 655,360 to 8,294,400 pixels

native_settings.name: quality
native_settings.values: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, auto (default auto); xhigh and max exist only on the 2.5 models

native_settings.name: background
native_settings.values: transparent, opaque, auto (default auto); transparent needs output_format png or webp

native_settings.name: output_format
native_settings.values: png (default), jpeg, webp

native_settings.name: output_compression
native_settings.values: 0 to 100 (compression level), for JPEG and WebP only

native_settings.name: moderation
native_settings.values: auto (default), low

native_settings.name: input_fidelity
native_settings.values: gpt-image-1.5: low or high. gpt-image-2: omit it; image inputs are always processed at high fidelity. gpt-image-2.5: not stated in the pages read.

native_settings.name: responses tool
native_settings.values: Responses API image_generation tool: action auto, generate or edit (edit an image already in the conversation); partial_images 1 to 3; the examples use gpt-image-2.5-sunburst

native_settings.name: images.edit parameters
native_settings.values: image (file or list), prompt, mask, model, n, size, quality, background, output_format, output_compression, input_fidelity (GPT Image 1.5), partial_images (streaming)

limitations: Text rendering and precise placement in layouts are listed as limitations by the vendor.
The gpt-image-2 cookbook (older) uses the same kind of labelled structure; its examples target gpt-image-2, not 2.5.
The ChatGPT product interface was not read.

targets.name: FLUX 3 Image

prompt_style.text: Medium and style first, then the subjects and where they sit, then light, colour and background: the FLUX 3 launch captions follow roughly this order, and the template is not a strict formula. Only what can be seen: no 'beautiful', 'iconic' or 'masterpiece'. A short prompt works because FLUX 3 Image expands it before it generates; add detail only for what you want to control.

negative_prompt.text: On FLUX 3 Image there is no negative_prompt, seed, prompt_upsampling or guidance field. Unknown fields return HTTP 422.

text_in_image.text: Quote each piece of text exactly, say where it goes and give it a type style. Without boxes, write the position in words.

references.text: images takes 1 to 10 references (URL or base64), each 256x256 px to 16 MP. The prompt says what to do with each image: edit, restyle or combine. There is no separate mode field.

edit.text: Send the image in images with a prompt that describes the change. A single edit does not need a box: FLUX 3 Image expands the instruction, may add a box for the element you name, and returns the expanded prompt, including any boxes, in result.prompt. To control exactly which elements change, use bounding boxes.

layout_boxes.text: Boxes are written into prompt: the description first, then a JSON array of rows {id, bbox, desc}, with bbox [top, left, bottom, right] as integers from 0 to 1000 measured from the top-left corner. The example is prompt = caption + ' ' + json.dumps(rows).

native_settings.name: safety_tolerance
native_settings.values: integer 0 (strictest) to 4; default 2

native_settings.name: grounding
native_settings.values: boolean, default true (web and image search before generating); false gives faster results from the prompt alone

native_settings.name: boxes
native_settings.values: appended after the caption as a JSON array of {id, bbox, desc} rows; bbox is [top, left, bottom, right] in integers from 0 to 1000; the caption names each element as <id>

native_settings.name: box rows: from
native_settings.values: a row with from: "ref_image_1" takes an element from a named reference image; the rest of the prompt describes the scene

limitations: The API is asynchronous; poll polling_url until the status is Ready.
A reference larger than 16 MP is refused (HTTP 400).

targets.name: FLUX.2 [pro] and [flex]

access.api: API reference pages exist for [pro] and [flex]; field names were not read

prompt_style.text: Use Subject + Action + Style + Context, most important first. Length bands: 10 to 30 words for quick exploration, 30 to 80 for most projects, 80 or more for complex scenes. Longer does not mean better.

negative_prompt.text: FLUX.2 has no negative prompts. Say what you want: 'sharp focus throughout' instead of 'no blur'; 'an empty scene' instead of 'no people'.

text_in_image.text: Put exact text in quotation marks and specify its placement and style.

references.text: Not read for FLUX.2 in this pass.

edit.text: The editing example pairs a prompt with input_image and an optional second image for multi-reference edits. The page was read only in part.

native_settings.name: hex colour in prompt
native_settings.values: tie each hex code to a specific object: 'the car is #FF0000'

native_settings.name: JSON prompt
native_settings.values: structured JSON is accepted directly or flattened into prose

native_settings.name: families
native_settings.values: [klein]: sub-second, open weights (4B Apache 2.0, 9B FLUX NCL); [pro]: production scale; [flex]: fine-grained control; [max]: maximum quality and grounding search; [dev]

native_settings.name: width and height
native_settings.values: integers in the request; the text-to-image example uses width 1024 and height 1024. Other request fields are not listed on the page read.

limitations: The FLUX.2 [klein] section says prose beats keyword lists and lighting matters most. It was read only in a summary, so it is not listed as verified.
No API field names are listed: the reference was not read.

targets.name: FLUX.1 Kontext (previous generation)

prompt_style.text: For edits, describe only what should change, because the input image supplies the rest of the scene. State what to preserve, use specific verbs, and spell out each change when several are made.

negative_prompt.text: No negative field is documented on the Kontext editing page.

text_in_image.text: Put the original and the replacement text in quotation marks, for example 'Sync & Bloom' changed to 'FLUX & JOY'.

references.text: Only one input image is documented for editing.

edit.text: Editing needs an instruction and an input image, sent to /v1/flux-kontext-pro.

native_settings.name: endpoint
native_settings.values: /v1/flux-kontext-pro

native_settings.name: aspect_ratio
native_settings.values: override only; ratios from 3:7 to 7:3; by default the output matches the input size rounded to multiples of 32

native_settings.name: input_image
native_settings.values: base64 or URL; up to 20 MB or 20 megapixels

limitations: The overview page calls Kontext [pro] a previous-generation model and recommends FLUX.2 for editing and generation.
Use Kontext only when a Kontext workflow is already in place.

targets.name: Ideogram 4.5 (API v2)

access.ui: Ideogram website (main site returned HTTP 403 when fetched)

prompt_style.text: A natural-language prompt is rewritten or expanded by magic_prompt (auto by default); a structured JSON prompt is used as written. JSON schema (4.5 and 4.0): high_level_description (required), style_description (optional), compositional_deconstruction with background and elements (required). bbox is [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] on 0 to 1000; palettes take up to 16 colours overall and 5 per element, as uppercase #RRGGBB.

negative_prompt.text: Neither the generate nor the precise-edit reference has a negative field. Exclusions must be written as positive description.

text_in_image.text: Put the exact words in quotation marks and say where they sit; name the text early in the prompt; keep the text short and the scene simple. Fonts cannot be picked by name, so describe the lettering. For several text blocks, describe them in reading order, or use a JSON prompt with text elements for exact placement. English works best; non-Latin scripts and accents can fail (Image app docs, 4.5 and 4.0). The API documentation pages do not state this rendering behaviour, so it is not assumed for the API.

references.text: Generation with source images takes up to 5 images, up to 25 MB each (JPEG, PNG or WEBP). The first image is the one edited; the others are extra references.

edit.text: Precise edit: the image to edit (up to 50 MB, raw bytes), an instruction in prompt, optional reference_images and mask. The result keeps the image's width and height. context_window confines the edit to one region.

native_settings.name: prompt
native_settings.values: 1 to 10000 characters, natural language or structured JSON

native_settings.name: magic_prompt
native_settings.values: auto (default), on, off

native_settings.name: resolution
native_settings.values: auto, source, or an exact WIDTHxHEIGHT; without source images an exact size must be a 1K or 2K preset (for example 1024x1024, 2048x2048, 1440x2880); with source images, auto is the default

native_settings.name: rendering_quality
native_settings.values: very_low, low, medium, high; default high without source images, medium with them; very_low needs source images

native_settings.name: background
native_settings.values: auto, transparent, opaque (the reference does not state a default)

native_settings.name: num_images
native_settings.values: integer, optional: number of images (API reference, no range given). The Image app allows Auto or 1 to 8 images per run

native_settings.name: seed
native_settings.values: integer, optional: random seed for reproducible generation (API reference). The Image app's Seed field takes digits up to 2147483647; the API range is not stated

native_settings.name: context_window
native_settings.values: none (default), auto (needs a mask), or four integers y_min,x_min,y_max,x_max

native_settings.name: logo guidance
native_settings.values: exact name in quotation marks; flat, minimal or badge style in plain words; two or three colours; one icon and one or two text lines; for a transparent PNG, the Ideogram 4.0 Transparent model in the Image app

native_settings.name: reference images in the Image app
native_settings.values: Auto takes up to 10; Ideogram 4.5 up to 5; Ideogram 4.0 and 3.0 none. With references, 4.5 reads the prompt as an edit instruction and hides Magic Prompt

limitations: Image URLs in responses expire; download results you want to keep.
Ideogram 4.0 has its own endpoint pages; its fields were not compared with 4.5 here.
Ideogram 3.0 has style presets, style reference images, negative prompts and colour palettes in the Image app (models page, UI). Those are not API claims for 4.5.
The Image app also runs partner models (GPT Image 2.5, Nano Banana 2 and Pro, Z-Image); this is product behaviour, not an Ideogram API fact.

targets.name: Recraft (V4.1 default)

access.ui: Recraft Studio (negative prompt field and an 'Avoid text in image' switch)

prompt_style.text: If the model does not read the prompt as expected, try a more general style (Recraft V3, Photorealism, Illustration) instead of a custom or niche style.

negative_prompt.text: The Studio has a negative prompt field. Write the unwanted item as a plain noun ('apples', not 'no apples'): the Studio page says 'no' can confuse the model. The API negative_prompt field is listed under native settings.

text_in_image.text: The Studio switch 'Avoid text in image' turns text generation off. The API equivalent is not confirmed.

references.text: style_references (multipart) and style_reference_urls (up to 10 image URLs) carry style references on the models that take them; the style is matched with style_match, flexible or precise (V4.1 model page)

edit.text: Three editing endpoints are documented on the endpoints page: POST /v1/images/imageToImage, POST /v1/images/inpaint and POST /v1/images/outpaint. The image-to-image page says it works with Recraft V3, V4 and V4.1, and that strength sets how far the result moves from the original. Prompt-based editing in the Studio is not covered here.

native_settings.name: model
native_settings.values: recraftv4_1 (default, raster); names ending in _vector return SVG; _raster aliases; V4.1 Flash is raster and takes no style; style references switch the default to recraftv4_styles

native_settings.name: style
native_settings.values: curated styles. The V4.1 model page lists style among the fields 'Not supported by V4.1' (with negative_prompt, text_layout, artistic_level and no_text). The endpoint reference says all models except V4.1 Flash. The pages disagree, so the renderer does not send style for recraftv4_1.

native_settings.name: negative_prompt
native_settings.values: V2 and V3 models only; V4.1 does not take negative_prompt (V4.1 model page: not supported by V4.1)

native_settings.name: text_layout
native_settings.values: V3 models only

native_settings.name: image_format
native_settings.values: webp (lossless) or png; ignored for vector output, which is always SVG

native_settings.name: random_seed
native_settings.values: integer, all models

native_settings.name: style_match and style_reference_urls
native_settings.values: style_reference_urls takes up to 10 image URLs; style_match is flexible or precise

limitations: The endpoint reference is long; only the fields named above were checked.
Compare the negative field behaviour on the model you use before relying on it.

targets.name: Seedream 5.0 (BytePlus ModelArk)

access.api: BytePlus ModelArk image generation API (named in a secondary summary)

prompt_style.text: The Seedream 4.0 and 4.5 prompt guide: if a particular style is needed, use precise style keywords or reference images. For edits, use concise, unambiguous instructions, avoid vague pronouns, and say what should stay unchanged.

negative_prompt.text: No negative_prompt field appears in the request fields of the API reference page read (image-generation-api.md, 2026-10-14). Absence on one page; not confirmed on other pages.

references.text: Seedream 5.0 pro and flash: up to 10 reference images; Seedream 5.0 lite, 4.5 and 4.0: up to 14. The batch mode (sequential) with several references keeps the total of inputs and outputs at 15 or fewer.

edit.text: Seedream 5.0 pro and flash: interactive editing by coordinates, selection boxes and arrows; the editing guide marks regions with <bbox> tags in the prompt.

targets.name: ComfyUI node graph

prompt_style.text: Text-to-image in ComfyUI takes two text inputs: a positive prompt (what you want) and a negative prompt (what you don't want), both encoded by the CLIP Text Encoder and connected to the KSampler. Write them as two separate blocks.

negative_prompt.text: The Negative condition input of the KSampler carries the negative prompt; the page explains it suppresses unwanted content.

text_in_image.text: Depends on the checkpoint in the graph.

references.text: Depends on the nodes in the graph; not covered by this entry.

edit.text: Depends on the workflow; not covered by this entry.

native_settings.name: cfg
native_settings.values: classifier-free guidance scale on the sampler node; controls prompt constraint strength (too high overfits)

native_settings.name: checkpoint
native_settings.values: the model file loaded by the checkpoint loader node; node values depend on it

native_settings.name: denoise
native_settings.values: image to image: the KSampler denoise is below 1; a lower value keeps more of the reference, and 0 stops sampling; denoise 1 starts from random noise

limitations: The text-to-image page's examples are for SD 1.5, not for newer models.
The FLUX.1 tutorial in ComfyUI says FLUX.1 does not need negative prompts; that is for FLUX.1 in ComfyUI, not for FLUX 3.
